message:
Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead:

A single central 800 kg Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), is a poor lift and a single-point detuning risk so I split it into a twin pair at midspan. In plain words two smaller masses do the same push-back but each can be hoisted from below and balance left to right. The rule that the damper can be bolted to the structure in the most effective location and custom designed to fit in the available space within or underneath the structure is stated in the Retrofitting Eagles Meadow Bridge with a Tuned Mass Damper (E46), and the precedent of two dampers with 500 kg combined moving mass installed at midspan adjacent to the two main girders concealed within the structure is described in the | Pedestrian Bridge Vibration |  |  | (E47). Each unit is 400 kg from the per-unit mass split (E52) weighing 3.92 kN from the per-unit weight calculation (E53), totalling 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) against 600 kN crowd load from the live-load estimate (E30), about five adults per lift versus hundreds on the deck.

Below-deck clearance governs so all moving steel stays between the girders above the bottom flange with nothing on the walkway. In plain words the deck look does not change because the device hides in the shadow of the structure. The free-decay simulation (E17) gives 49.4 mm peak relative travel so my caged stops give an 80 mm clear gap with elastomer pads plus lockable service pins as shown in the twin under-deck layout sketch (E55), which fits inside a hand width and well inside girder depth.

Tuning and maintenance must happen without closing the deck using access from below and tolerant tuning. In plain words the fitter tunes from a platform underneath not through the footway and spaced tunes ride out drift. The finding that a Multiple Tuned Mass Damper system demonstrates stronger robustness when dealing with random pedestrian loads is stated in the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), and the rule that girders shall be made accessible from the ground, from walkways within the girder bays, or by a Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), is stated in the Bridge Design Manual Section 2 (E49). The High-Strength Friction-Grip clamped cross-beam, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), carries the 5.22 kN peak dynamic force from the dynamic-force calculation (E29) cycling at 1.9 Hz, about seven body weights, which governs loosening not strength.

My position is not ready, because the Manager has not yet chosen between one central mass and the twin distributed pair and the access route needs agreement.
